biggest_gap.title: Kernel Money adds base amounts that were already rounded, against the owner-signed rounding rule, so foreign-currency documents can be off by fils
biggest_gap.detail: Every module that posts foreign-currency amounts (purchases in USD or EUR, the everyday case for a UAE trading company) will build on the kernel Money type. docs/compliance/vat-rounding-and-currency.md rule 2, signed off by the owner, says: 'Rounding happens once, on the figure that is stated. Lines and tax-category subtotals keep their full precision; the invoice total is rounded to 2 decimals.' The kernel breaks this in two ways. (a) Money.Create rounds each base amount to the fils, and Money.Add sums those rounded amounts (BaseAmount + other.BaseAmount). Example: three lines of USD 1.00 at 3.6725 give 3.67 + 3.67 + 3.67 = AED 11.01, but the rule gives 11.0175, rounded to 11.02. (b) Money.Create throws on any amount with more decimals than the currency's minor units, so a line cannot keep full precision at all. Round 9 reported this and it is still open (round 10 only factored out RoundToMinorUnits). Fix in the kernel before p08 and the ledger build on it: keep line and subtotal base amounts at full precision (or carry the unrounded product), round only the stated total, and have the type report the rounding difference that e-invoices put in 'Rounding Amount'. This is a rule already signed off, so implementing it needs no new human gate.
biggest_gap.evidence: git show c4cfacb:src/Kernel/Erp.Kernel/Money/Money.cs: line 93 throws when an amount has more decimals than the currency's minor units, line 96 rounds the base amount on creation, line 117 'BaseAmount + other.BaseAmount'. Compare with git show c4cfacb:docs/compliance/vat-rounding-and-currency.md, Rule 2. To reproduce in any test: var l = Money.Create(1.00m, USD, 3.6725m, AED); l.Add(l).Add(l).BaseAmount == 11.01m, while rule 2 gives 11.02m.
